### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **65** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**64** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 38 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 41 pages)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **153** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b227d7415381da4f6c3744e94dd2d71b81588698` — the merge of head `cd6fe0b4fbeb9c1b50160a05d6972197daf647cb` into base `2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b227d7415381da4f6c3744e94dd2d71b81588698 && git checkout b227d7415381da4f6c3744e94dd2d71b81588698
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3 cd6fe0b4fbeb9c1b50160a05d6972197daf647cb && git checkout -B drift-repro 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3 && git merge --no-ff cd6fe0b4fbeb9c1b50160a05d6972197daf647cb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cd6fe0b4fbeb9c1b50160a05d6972197daf647cb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-identity-email.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-log-objects.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/outbox-sweep.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/attachment-reclaim.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/attachment-storage.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/internal-header-readback.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, .changeset/24531-identity-mail-sibling.md

Reviewer: an isolated at-tier reviewer subagent of the adopting seat (`epic:#15194`). Face: schema (`reviewFace` on the PR's file list hits `packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts` and `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`), so the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line is not itself a face. Read-only: the net diff `origin/main...refs/review/pr-24587` (27 files, +1111/-291), the card #24531 with 6267492651, 6270006270 and 6270136912, the rulings 6266750393, 6267391172, 6270035914, the decision 6257510973 (Q2 A), step 0's plan 6268559156 (`step_plan.steps[2]`, F1-F3), the merged harness `packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts` and its fixture, AGENTS.md, `scripts/check-changeset-*.mjs`, and the head's check-runs. The head did not move during the review (re-resolved at the end: `cd6fe0b4f`). The PR body's verification section names `3bc88f5f1`; the addendum 6270136912 is the harness run on `cd6fe0b4f` (one merge of `main` later), which is the head reviewed here.

**Check-runs on `cd6fe0b4f`: 41 runs, 36 success, 5 skipped, 0 failure.** Skipped: Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate shards (1-3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke — all off the per-PR path by `ci.yml`'s event deny-list (the aggregate `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded success with zero legs). Green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates (every lane), Spec property liveness, Test Core (6/6), the four Type Check lanes, Build Core, Build Docs, the three claim/branch guards. No governed path in the file list (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/workflows/**`).

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Fresh install — every identity send lands in the sibling, with no organization. HOLDS.**
- The five sends at four sites in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` each say `identityMail: true` and name no `organizationId`: password reset `:2048` and account invitation `:2033` (one `sendResetPassword` callback, branched on `invitation`), verification `:2113`, magic link `:4131`, email-change notice `:5977`. `authMailOrganizationArg` / `derivableWriteOrganizationId` are deleted, so no identity send can regain an organization by the old path.
- The organization invitation `:3888-3890` is untouched: it threads `invitation.organizationId` and carries no `identityMail`, so it stays in `sys_email`.
- Routing is decided once per send in `email-service.ts:752` (`emailLogObjectOf`, `:237`) and every write of that send carries it: insert `:820`, `updateRow` on the sent and failed branches, the queue payload `:1103`, the reclaim job, the rejection record `:911`. `sendTemplate` forwards the flag `:1511`. Template resolution is by `(name, locale)` only (`SendTemplateInput.organizationId` is pass-through to the row stamp, `packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts:222-240`), so routing identity mail organization-less under `single` changes which table the row lands in and nothing about which template renders.
- `identityMail: true` beside an `organizationId` is refused as `VALIDATION_FAILED` before normalisation (`:711`, `:247`) and the refusal is recorded in the sibling without the organization (`:925`). Contract-first: no silent drop, no silent win.
- The sibling (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-identity-email.object.ts`) declares `systemFields: { tenant: false }` `:45`, `sys_email`'s fields and indexes held equal by `sys-identity-email.object.test.ts`, `managedBy: 'append-only'`, `apiMethods: ['get','list']` `:240`. Registered beside `sys_email` by `EmailServicePlugin` (`email-plugin.ts:406`), so boot-time schema sync creates it (F1: the boot path only adds). Named in `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` (`platform-object-names.ts:55`) and the regenerated tenancy census (84 registered, 40 out of reach).
- Pins: `identity-mail-sibling.test.ts` drives reset, verification, magic link and change-email under `single`, walled and no-tenancy-service postures and asserts the flag present and `organizationId` absent, with the organization invitation as the non-vacuity control; `email-plugin.outbox-sweep.test.ts` (new describe blocks after `:605`) pins a fresh send into the sibling with no `organization_id` key and `sys_email` empty, the tenant control, and the refusal record; `send-template.test.ts` pins both writes naming `sys_identity_email`; the dogfood census (`signup-organization-census.dogfood.test.ts`) asserts the sign-up's verification mail is in `sys_identity_email`, absent from `sys_email`, and that the registered schema of the sibling has no `organization_id` with `sys_email`'s as the control. The PR body's fresh showcase boot reports one reset row and one verification row in the sibling, the invite-member row in `sys_email`.
- Gap, non-blocking: `identity-mail-sibling.test.ts` drives the reset branch only; `auth.account_invitation` (same callback, `invitation` set) is changed identically in the diff but is not driven by any test. Suggest one more drive with `invitation` set.

**(b) 18.0 database — every outbox reader covers both tables. HOLDS.** The two logs are named once in `email-log-objects.ts:22-46`; `emailLogObjectOfJob` reads absent as `sys_email` (every 18.0 job), a log name as that log, anything else as `undefined`, which every caller refuses loudly.
- Drain hook `email-plugin.ts:752`: `isEmailLogObject(object)` admits both logs; the re-read `:766` and `deliverPersistedRow` carry the hook's object.
- Queue consumer `email-plugin.ts:840`: `emailLogObjectOfJob(data?.object)`; a `{ rowId }` job with no `object` reads `sys_email` (pinned: "an 18.0 { rowId } job with no object reads sys_email and delivers that row"); a job naming a non-log is refused at `error` and touches no row (pinned). A `sys_email` job keeps the exact 18.0 payload `email-service.ts:1103`, and the idempotency key for a `sys_email` row stays `sys_email:rowId` `:1117`, so a sweep re-publish of an 18.0 queued row still collapses onto its pending 18.0 job.
- Boot sweep `email-plugin.ts:1008`: `for (const object of EMAIL_LOG_OBJECTS)`, each log swept on its own with its own error line, results summed (`sumSweepResults` carries all six fields of `OutboxSweepResult`). `outbox-sweep.ts:183/:191/:220/:227` thread the object. Pinned: the 18.0 identity row seeded into `sys_email` is delivered in place and nothing moves to the sibling.
- Attachment reclaim `attachment-reclaim.ts:199`: `emailLogObjectOfJob(payload?.object)`; `find` `:220` and the `update` `:273-274` name it; a job naming a non-log stalls without re-arm and without the row-gone delete branch (pinned). The re-arm `email-plugin.ts:919-925` republishes the same payload, so `object` survives a re-arm; the reclaim idempotency key for `sys_email` rows is unchanged.
- Header readback `internal-header-readback.ts:107/:143`: per-call object; the `internal: true` flag is on the sibling's `headers_json` `:136`, and the engine's redaction and `resolveInternalField` are keyed on that flag, not on the object name (`objectql/src/engine.ts:11281-11290`, `core/src/utils/internal-write-response.ts:129`), so the sibling inherits the omission on the generic data path.
- Readers hunted and not missed: a grep of the whole tree at the head for engine reads of `'sys_email'` outside plugin-email finds none; no file outside plugin-email imports `OUTBOX_OBJECT`, `RECLAIM_OBJECT`, `SYS_EMAIL_OBJECT` or the new constants; plugin-auth has no rate limiter or resend cooldown that counts mail rows (its remaining `sys_email` mentions are comments and the invitation stamp); no Setup nav entry, page or list view names `sys_email` (only translation echo tests); the console (`objectui`) reads `sys_email` only as the `source_object` label of an activity item. The audit mirror (`plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`) is generic per object (`enable.activities !== false`, `sys_email` is not in `SKIP_OBJECTS`), so `sys_identity_email` writes are ledgered and mirrored by construction, under Q3 A's derivation (Default Organization under `single`, no row under a wall) — the dogfood census asserts the resulting `sys_activity` rows name the Default Organization.
- F3 (select by shape, never NULL): no reader selects by `organization_id IS NULL`; every read is by table, id or status. The stamped 18.0 rows stay in `sys_email` and keep being delivered, swept and reclaimed.

**(c) Access — who may read the sibling. HOLDS.** `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']` `:46` is a top-level object key (ADR-0066 D3). On `main`, plugin-security enforces it as the AND-gate before the CRUD grant for every non-system caller holding permission sets (`security-plugin.ts:2678-2725`); a caller with no sets falls to the CRUD check, which no grant satisfies (fail-closed). The system context bypasses the middleware (`security-plugin.ts:2388`), which is how the pipeline's `SYSTEM_CTX` reads and writes both logs and how `sys_job` already works. The capability is `scope: 'platform'` (`spec/src/security/capabilities.ts:48`), so no tenant administrator holds it by role — the `deployment-level-no-tenant-column.test.ts` roster pins that for `sys_job` and its siblings. `/meta` exposes the schema (fields, `requiredPermissions`), no rows. `headers_json` stays omitted on the generic read path (above). Net: the sibling is strictly tighter than `sys_email`, whose reads stay open — the dev's filed observation that 18.0 identity rows in `sys_email` carry reset links behind no `requiredPermissions` is pre-existing and outside this card (③).

**(d) Nothing moves or deletes 18.0 rows. HOLDS.** No migration, no data move, no column change on `sys_email`; `RECLAIM_OBJECT`, `OUTBOX_OBJECT` and `SYS_EMAIL_OBJECT` keep their values. The inventory row for `sys_identity_email` (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts:547-552`, fate `column-drop`, `PMAIN`) is inert on an 18.0 database: `dropColumnsThroughDrift` acts only on `drop_column` drift entries, and a table that never had the column produces none. The boot guard (F2) flags only a `tenant: false` object with a physical `organization_id`; the sibling is created fresh without one on both a fresh install and an 18.0 database. Harness test 3 (every reshaped row keeps its key columns, including the fixture's two stamped `sys_email` rows) passed on this head per 6270136912.

**(e) R1-R4.** The addendum reports the harness 8/8 on `cd6fe0b4f`: R1 and R2 boot, the fixture's people sign in, R2 data, R3 refused. R4 is not in the harness (no walled case). Judgement: it does not matter for this PR. The diff touches no posture or boot-guard code; the walled refusal lives in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:6266` (`walledPostureRefusal`) and is pinned by `serve-walled-posture-refusal.test.ts`, which Test Core ran green on this head. R4 therefore holds by construction and by CI. The missing walled case is a step-0 harness gap for the seat, not a defect of this card (step 4 rewrites that case anyway). Two notes: the harness evidence is the dev's local run, since `ci.yml` keeps the dogfood shards off the per-PR and merge-group paths and the opt-in lane (#24554) is open Tier H; and the plan's `pr_cut.proof` wanted a harness case for "the 18.0 reset row is still readable through the outbox's dual read" — the claim (6267492651) forbade touching #24522's harness files, so the PR pins it at unit level instead (`email-plugin.outbox-sweep.test.ts`, 18.0-shaped `sys_email` fixture plus a raw `{ rowId }` job). Acceptable at this tier.

**(f) Complete feature (6270035914). HOLDS.** New installs write the new shape, the 18.0 shape is still read, and nothing waits on a later PR: the object, the contract member, the five producers, the five readers, the gate, the inventory row, the census and the docs land together, exercised end to end on the real stack by the dogfood census. No dormant code: `identityMail` is consumed by `send()`, the constants are used, the exports are the plugin's public names for the two logs.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` at the start of a line in both the PR body and the committed changeset `.changeset/24531-identity-mail-sibling.md`; `readClause2Line` reads `declared`, arm `widening`. The arm matches the diff: a new object, a new optional contract member on `SendEmailInput` and `SendTemplateInput`, optional trailing parameters on `EmailPersistence.insert`/`update`/`readHeadersJson`, `deliverPersistedRow`, `enqueuePersistedRow`, `sweepStrandedOutbox` and `OutboxSweepService`, a new optional `object` member on both queue payloads, and five new exports — every existing caller and implementer compiles unchanged, and every existing value (`SYS_EMAIL_OBJECT`, `OUTBOX_OBJECT`, `RECLAIM_OBJECT`, the `sys_email` job payload and idempotency keys) is preserved. No accept set narrows; no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. The changeset grades `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-email` and `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `minor` (the level axis: at least one published source moved `minor` — four are) and `@objectstack/cli` `patch` (one inventory row); no `major`, so the launch-window guard is quiet; `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The body states the before/now/remedy for a reader of `sys_email` and names the touched surfaces; no release-owned file (`content/docs/releases/`, `CHANGELOG.md`) is edited. `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx` is a hand edit of a non-generated page; the tenant-audit census page and counts file are regenerated outputs. Spec touched: no generated artifact is stale (Lint & Repo Gates and Spec property liveness green).

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Decided open questions (6270006270), all consistent with Q2 A:** name `sys_identity_email` + `identityMail` (A); refuse `identityMail` + `organizationId` and record the rejection (A); reads behind `manage_platform_settings` (A); identity mail is deployment-level in every posture, so under `single` it no longer carries the Default Organization (A — the ruling says deployment-level "by un-mixing", not "under a wall only"). No question is left for the seat.
2. **`ceremony_owes` (the step-5 identity-mail move), recorded table by table and matching the plan's `ceremony_must_later`:** move terminal identity rows out of `sys_email` without `organization_id`; rewrite or drain pending `{ rowId }` send jobs and no-`object` reclaim jobs first (a moved row's reclaim job would take the row-gone branch and delete content); re-point or delete `sys_activity` rows about moved mail; 8e NOT NULL on `sys_email.organization_id` only after the move leaves zero NULL rows; step 7 keeps the no-`object`-reads-`sys_email` default for tenant jobs. One refinement for the step-5 card: the plan's selector ("related_object = 'sys_user' or template, not NULL") does not cover the magic-link rows, which carry no `related_object` (auth-manager `:4127-4131` sends none) and `sys_email` has no template column — the ceremony must define their shape (or leave them) before it moves anything. F3's single-posture rows are stamped with the Default Organization; whether they move is the ceremony's decision, as the dev notes.
3. **Harness evidence is local, by design of `ci.yml`:** the dogfood shards (which hold the harness and the modified census test) run only on `push` and schedule; the per-PR label lane is #24554, open Tier H. The 8/8 on `cd6fe0b4f` is the addendum's. If the head moves before landing, the seat must have the harness re-run on the new head; this record names `cd6fe0b4f` only.
4. **ADR-0131 D7 already carries the dated Q2 A note (`docs/adr/0131-…md:538-546`), so Prime Directive #13 is satisfied; its closing "it has not shipped" needs the dated update once this lands — Tier H, the maintainer's PR, off this card.** Cloud's wall-test non-vacuity control is rewritten against the sibling in the cloud lane (per the ruling).
5. **Pre-existing exposure, out of scope:** `sys_email` declares no `requiredPermissions`, and 18.0 identity rows there carry reset links; whether a non-administrator can list them was not measured by the dev (filed as an observation, no card). Strictly outside this card's surface; the seat may want a follow-up card.
6. **Non-blocking suggestions:** add `sys_identity_email` to the hand-kept `DEPLOYMENT_LEVEL` roster in `packages/platform-objects/src/deployment-level-no-tenant-column.test.ts` (the PR's own test asserts the same three facts, so nothing is unpinned); drive the `auth.account_invitation` branch in `identity-mail-sibling.test.ts`.
